glosses: Having the strength exhausted by toil or exertion; tired; fatigued.

examples.text: A weary traveller knocked at the door.
I care not for my spirits if my legs were not weary.
[I] am weary, thinking of your task.
There was a neat hat-and-umbrella stand, and the stranger's weary feet fell soft on a good, serviceable dark-red drugget, which matched in colour the flock-paper on the walls.
With the lift in the block still out of order, they climbed the flights and flights of steps. When Dad finally put the key in the front door, both were weary beyond words.

glosses: Having one's patience, relish, or contentment exhausted; tired; sick.

examples.text: soldiers weary of marching, or of confinement;  I grew weary of studying and left the library.

glosses: Expressive of fatigue.

examples.text: He gave me a weary smile.

glosses: Causing weariness; tiresome.

examples.text: And now she was vppon the weary way,
There passed a weary time.
She had to dance all night without resting till break of day […] Old women supported her in the weary task, and they all danced together, arm in arm.

glosses: To make or to become weary.

examples.text: So shall he waste his means, weary his soldiers,
I would not cease / To wearie him with my assiduous cries.

His name was Henderland; he spoke with the broad south-country tongue, which I was beginning to weary for the sound of; and besides common countryship, we soon found we had a more particular bond of interest.

Next morning, as I stood motionless and with heavy eyes at the helm—for I had not slept well—I began to weary anxiously for daylight, and peered towards the horizon, where I thought I observed something like a black cloud against the dark sky.

Yet there was no time to be lost if I was ever to get out alive, and so I groped with my hands against the side of the grave until I made out the bottom edge of the slab, and then fell to grubbing beneath it with my fingers. But the earth, which the day before had looked light and loamy to the eye, was stiff and hard enough when one came to tackle it with naked hands, and in an hour's time I had done little more than further weary myself and bruise my fingers.

glosses: Bored to the point of weariness.

examples.text: The boy was sick and tired of doing his lengthy homework assignment.

glosses: Annoyed or frustrated with something or someone, to the point of losing one's temper or patience.

examples.text: She was sick and tired of her daughter pestering her to help her with her homework.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see sick, tired.

examples.text: I'm feeling both sick and tired right now.

glosses: Qui ressent de l'ennui.

examples.text: Un malentendu existe entre lui et les simples mortels. […]. Son ironie naturelle les gène et les déconcerte. Il est ennuyé, blasé ; […].
